messages:
Megan (sre): heads up — we're getting a sustained p99 504 spike for tenant acme-corp on hosted inference. Customer reports timeouts from 12:03 - intermittent but tail is huge.
Megan (sre): Observable: request_queue.depth peaked at 10240, continuous_batcher.backlog ~ 8200, dequeue latency p99 > 6s.
Jess (support): customer says they see 504s in their webhook retries. They're on standard hosted tier.
Raj (eng-runtime): any change in traffic pattern? longseq or many short requests?
Megan (sre): mix: high fanout of small prompts but lots of concurrent sessions. Sequence lengths are small but KV cache warmups causing batches to stall.
ops-bot: incident created INC-945: assigned to eng-runtime.
Raj (eng-runtime): looking at batcher metrics — several continuous batcher threads stuck in warmup for the same model shard, causing in-flight batches to queue.
Raj (eng-runtime): quick repro query: ```
# check queue and batcher stats
curl -s "http://metrics.internal/api/queues?tenant=acme-corp" | jq '.queues|{depth:.depth, backlog:.continuous_backlog, inflight:.inflight}'
```
Megan (sre): results show: { depth: 10240, backlog: 8200, inflight: 128 }
Jess (support): sent customer a status update. They asked for ETA.
Raj (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation options: 1) lower continuous_batcher.max_batch_size for model-x to 8, 2) increase dequeue_workers for hosted pool by +20%, 3) temporarily route acme-corp to dedicated pool if available.
Megan (sre): tried lowering max_batch_size on one node — dequeue lag improved locally, overall queue depth slowly falling.
Raj (eng-runtime): manual mitigation command: ```
# patch runtime config for model-x on pool hosted-3
rcli update-pool-config --pool hosted-3 --model model-x --set continuous_batcher.max_batch_size=8
rcli scale-pool --pool hosted-3 --workers +10
```
Megan (sre): also saw many small requests with identical prompt prefixes — enabling prefix caching cut duplicate compute for warmups. Suggest enabling prefix_cache.enabled=true for tenant.
Jess (support): customer accepted temporary routing to dedicated if we can give them an ETA.
Raj (eng-runtime): caution: routing to dedicated requires capacity; fallback if capacity not available will still hit fallback tier. Also increase tenant.max_inflight to avoid client-side retry amplification: ```
rcli set-tenant-limits --tenant acme-corp --max_inflight 200
```
Megan (sre): root cause hypothesis: continuous batcher threads were pinned on KV cache population due to many near-identical short requests that cause cache churn; backlog grew until queue depth hit soft limit and requests timed out at gateway.
Raj (eng-runtime): follow-ups: - add backpressure metric alert when continuous_backlog > 2000 for 2m - add auto-shrink of max_batch_size when dequeue latency p95 > 1s - add de-dup/enforce small-request prefix caching on ingress.
ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-saturation-cont-batch 
Jess (support): action items I committed to: notify customer with mitigation timeline, escalate contract support if dedicated routing needed.
Megan (sre): current status: after lowering batch_size + +10 workers, queue depth decreased to ~4200 and p99 504s dropped to baseline but still elevated. Monitoring continuing.
Raj (eng-runtime): next: roll the config to all hosted pools for model-x, and push a lightweight hotfix to reduce warmup locking in batcher (PR#7201).
Megan (sre): tagging this thread for postmortem. Please paste any traces/log snippets here.
Jess (support): customer update sent: "we've applied temporary measures; expect improved latency in 10-15m. Escalation open."
incident-bot: incident INC-945 status -> mitigated (partial).
Megan (sre): thanks team. We'll keep it open until steady for 1h, then close and write postmortem.
